answer: Price identity in clock time, not tokens. To register, a device-rooted secret must pass a verifiable delay function costing hours of sequential compute, and its nullifier is admitted once. Wanting a hundred voices, an operator must run a hundred unrelated delays: copied outputs are rejected and parallelism buys only more machines. A slashed bond can be recycled, but a spent delay evaporates, capping sybil supply by elapsed time. Each entry carries its own pearl of sequential proof, so honesty stands clear of the jetty of forged accounts, with no ivory veneer hiding a copied output.
